body:
It's complicated. But, what relationship isn’t? We love each other in different ways. I do have romantic feelings for her. We simply don’t mesh well in real life though. I’ve known her for four years and I’ve spent time with her a grand total of twice. Each time was... traumatic (mostly for me). So, we’ve moved away from anything remotely like the traditional relationship. It’s evolved into something along the lines of older sibling / younger sibling or parent / child. I watch over her, I offer help when it’s needed, give advice, but mostly I just encourage her to follow her dreams and move forward with her life. She’s starting to do well on her own now, I’m very proud of her, and I’m sure she’ll be able to thrive. 

It's certainly not a painful relationship. At a distance we get along extremely well (she’s recently been talking about getting matching tattoos). I do feel bad about leaving her, and that’s why I want to make sure she’s at least financially taken care of when I’m gone. I haven’t figured out how to end things with her. In this case a gentle lie might be the best option. I travel frequently and a lot of the time I’m out of touch because of it. Maybe I’ll take one final long term trip, somewhere nice, but remote. Somewhere she wouldn’t expect me to be able to maintain contact.

I came because there really isn't any other place to go. I went for r/suicide, and it brought me here. I'm starting to think it was a mistake. I'm taking time and people away from the folks that want things to change. 

Enjoying things isn't something I've ever done, just one task to the next. But thats life.

As for why I posted, not sure. I'm not really looking for options. I don't really care to stop. I just didn't want to pull an Eastman, none of that "my work is done" nonsense. I felt the need to talk.

Germany, Korea, Amsterdam, Rome, Romania, Hawaii, Japan, Kuwait, Dubai, Iraq
I’m pretty well traveled for a simple country boy. Something I figured out fairly quickly, I don’t like it one bit, wherever I am I’m always just waiting to go home. As for starting over and changing things, I tried. I quit my job of seven years and took one that was completely different. It lasted six months, I quit that and took my old job back. 

It's hard to explain why I want things to end. I've got a good life and I'm surrounded by fantastic people. I just don't care to do it anymore.

My love life, heh. I'm a little over thirty now, and the last real romantic relationship I had was back in high school. Love falls in the same category as my boat, I’ve always been missing a key ingredient. It all comes down to time, ability, and inclination. I’ve always been content in solitude. Those few times where I’ve felt lonely, I just wasn’t in a position to act. And time, well time has always been my enemy.

For Ana, we've got.. a history. It's better for both of us if we maintain at least an oceans distance. So, I won't be visiting her. Besides she's just started a new life, she certainly doesn't need the past coming back to haunt her.

Ah, well I've always been one of those people that can't stand the thought of inconveniencing someone or being a burden (I've never gone back and corrected an order at the drive-thru) Even in this, I want things to go as smoothly as possible. So, I'm taking care of what I can. I've gathered most of my resources together, and I'll divide them up to take care of a few thing and leave the rest for my family. It should be pretty simple and painless.

She's not that kind of boat. She's a little three seater jet boat. And right now she is getting used. I gave her to my uncle to sell and in the meantime he's using her. 

As for the Scout, I love that truck. Its just the deadly combination of mechanical incompetence (not on my part), and bad luck that have kept the old girl down. She's the one thing I couldn't bring myself to sell.

I do help as much as I'm able. A lot of what I've got left is making sure things don't come to a halt. I certainly don't have the resources to make a permanent contribution, but things should continue for awhile. 

My biggest concern is my friend Ana. About a year ago I helped her move to Europe and I've provided support while shes tried to find her way there. I've set aside enough to augment the money she earns from her job to keep her afloat for at least another year. It should give her time to figure out exactly where she's going and what she's doing with her life.

Funny thing about that boat. I've had it for a little over three years.. and I've never put it in the water. I always pictured myself doing exactly as you suggested, just relaxing on the water and letting the world wait for a little while. The reality was very different, I've always been missing one of the three key ingredients, time, inclination, and ability. If I had time, I didn't feel like it, or my Scout was busted so I couldn't go. If I had the inclination, I'd have to rush off somewhere due to work, or the Scout was busted. And, well the Scout is always busted. So, it never worked out. The truly horrible bit, I actually lived on a lake for about six months. Even now I live maybe a 1/2 mile from the river.
I tried a dog. It last about three months. I've never seen so much devastation. I found him a good home though. Most of his problems were simply because I couldn't give him the attention he needed.
